channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Macron Addresses French Citizens Firmly Amidst Widespread Riots
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron demanded tough government measures to prevent further large-scale street riots. He urged the cabinet to learn from intelligence services' shortcomings in gathering information and predicting incidents. Macron stated that nothing justifies the rioters' actions, expressing collective anger and shame. He announced a crisis unit led by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to find solutions and support victims, while emphasizing that protesters' voices must be heard and root causes addressed, upholding the rule of law.

item.title: New Bridge to Connect Samarkand Center with Shirin District and Airport
item.description: A modern bridge is under construction over the Karadarya River, connecting the center of Samarkand with the Shirin district and the international airport. The 780-meter-long bridge aims to optimize traffic flow, enhance safety, and reduce congestion. Upon completion, travel time from Shirin to the city center will be reduced by 30 minutes.

item.title: US and Central Asian Foreign Ministers to Meet in Samarkand for Economic and Security Talks
item.description: US Special Representative for South and Central Asia, discussed cooperation in critical minerals, energy, and agriculture with American companies. Secretary of State Antony Blinken arrived in Samarkand for meetings with foreign ministers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. The US aims to increase economic and security cooperation with the region.

item.title: Ministry Warns Citizens Against Unverified Job Offers Abroad
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection warns citizens about an increase in online advertisements offering quick employment abroad. The Migration Committee urges caution against scammers, noting that many offers come from unregistered foreign intermediaries. Citizens are advised to use only officially accredited operators for safe overseas employment.

item.title: Security Officials from Turkey, Qatar, and Russia Visit Kabul Amidst Regional Tensions
item.description: Senior security officials from Turkey, Qatar, and Russia have recently visited Kabul. These visits, including meetings with Taliban intelligence heads, occur amid heightened tensions between the Taliban and Pakistan, suggesting a focus on regional security dynamics and potential mediation efforts.

item.title: Human rights defenders urge UN to halt forced evictions in Omid-e Sabz Township
item.description: Human rights defenders and civil society organizations have appealed to the UN to stop the Taliban's forced evictions and land seizures in Omid-e Sabz Township. The letter highlights increased pressure on residents, predominantly Shia Hazaras, threatening their livelihoods and security. Approximately 80,000 people face displacement.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Welcomes US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to Uzbekistan
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, welcomed US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on his first visit to Uzbekistan. She expressed her pleasure at his arrival, marking a significant diplomatic engagement between the two nations. The visit underscores strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh Ministry of Labor Warns Citizens About Foreign Job Scams
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor has cautioned citizens about fraudulent job offers from abroad, often originating from unregistered foreign intermediaries. The ministry warns that pursuing easy money through such schemes can lead to significant financial losses and legal issues in a foreign country. Official accredited operators are recommended for secure international employment.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Visits Imam Bukhari Mausoleum in Samarkand
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev began his trip to Samarkand by visiting the memorial complex of Imam Bukhari. He emphasized the importance of preserving and promoting the great scholar's scientific heritage to attract global tourism and foster Islamic enlightenment. The complex, rebuilt on the president's initiative, is a major pilgrimage site.

item.title: Egypt Offers Support to Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks, President Sisi States
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi announced Egypt's readiness to support Saudi Arabia in response to Houthi attacks. Speaking on the country's alignment with directives from Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Sisi affirmed Egypt's commitment to regional stability and security.

item.title: Iran Appoints New Defense Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi with Parliamentary Support
item.description: Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi as the new defense minister, eight months after the previous minister's death during a joint US-Israeli attack. Akhlaghi secured 237 out of 277 votes. He replaces Aziz Nasirzadeh, who died on February 28, the same day as several high-ranking Iranian military officials.

item.title: US could become a more significant player in Central Asia, says former ambassador
item.description: Former US Ambassador to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, Daniel Rosenblum, believes the US can become a more significant player in Central Asia. He notes the unusual format of the current visit by the Secretary of State accompanied by a large business delegation. Rosenblum, who dedicated 28 years to US foreign policy focusing on the region, sees this as a positive development potentially leading to new successes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Warns Citizens About Fake Job Offers Abroad
item.description: Kazakhstan's Migration Committee advises citizens to be wary of enticing advertisements for quick employment abroad. Many offers come from unregistered foreign entities operating outside legal frameworks, leading to potential financial losses and difficulties for job seekers. The committee urges vigilance and verification of official operators for safe international employment.

item.title: US Secretary of State Rubio Arrives in Samarkand for Central Asia Talks
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Uzbekistan for high-level diplomatic talks with Central Asian foreign ministers. The meetings in Samarkand aim to establish a foundation for economic and security cooperation. Rubio emphasized the importance of strategic engagement beyond immediate crises, highlighting long-term diplomatic priorities.

item.title: US Secretary of State Rubio Arrives in Samarkand for Central Asia Talks
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Uzbekistan for high-level diplomatic talks with Central Asian foreign ministers. The meetings in Samarkand aim to establish a foundation for economic and security cooperation. Rubio emphasized the importance of strategic engagement beyond immediate crises, highlighting long-term diplomatic priorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Participates in SCO National Coordinators Meeting in Dushanbe
item.description: Kazakhstan's Special Envoy for SCO Affairs, Murat Mukushev, attended a meeting of national coordinators in Dushanbe. Discussions focused on trade, economic, and cultural-humanitarian cooperation within the SCO framework. Participants also reviewed draft documents on transport, financial cooperation, and improving the Organization's activities.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 630 People Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan Yesterday
item.description: The Taliban announced the forced return of 636 individuals, including 134 families, to Afghanistan via multiple border crossings. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that 421 people entered through Nimroz, with others arriving via Torkham and Spin Boldak. These returns occur amidst Afghanistan's severe economic crisis and poverty.

item.title: Afghan Migrants in Italy Face Low Wages and Discrimination, Report States
item.description: Migrants from Afghanistan in Italy face challenges including low wages, high living costs, exploitation, and hiring discrimination, according to the Afghanistan Analysts Network. Many jobs are seasonal and informal, leading some to seek higher wages elsewhere in Europe. Undeclared work contributes to exploitation, with safety regulations often ignored.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts SCO National Coordinators Meeting to Prepare for Prime Ministers' Summit
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a meeting of the Council of National Coordinators of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to prepare for the upcoming summit of the organization's heads of government on October 19-20. Discussions focused on transit-transport cooperation, financial collaboration, and improving the SCO's effectiveness.

item.title: US Secretary of State Mark Rubio's Plane Lands in Samarkand for C5+1 Summit
item.description: US Secretary of State Mark Rubio has arrived in Samarkand to participate in the C5+1 summit. He was welcomed by the head of the Presidential Administration, Saida Mirziyoyeva, and Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov. The summit focuses on regional cooperation and security issues involving Central Asian nations and the United States.

item.title: Central Asia and US Foreign Ministers to Meet in Uzbekistan for C5+1 Summit
item.description: The foreign ministers of Central Asian countries and the United States will convene in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on October 19 for the C5+1 format meeting. U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken will also hold bilateral meetings with representatives from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Weapons and grenades found near residential buildings in Almaty
item.description: Almaty police discovered a cache of weapons and ammunition hidden near private homes on Astrahan Street. The discovery was made during a special operation called 'Weapons'. The seized items included a TOZ-25 rifle, a pistol-like weapon, various ammunition, and sound grenades. A criminal case has been initiated, and the items sent for examination.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev inspects new bridge construction in Samarkand
item.description: During his visit to the Samarkand region, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the construction of a new bridge over the Karadarya River. The bridge will connect the 'Shirin' residential area with the city and the international airport, aiming to improve traffic flow and safety. The project costs 310 billion soums and will have a capacity of 25,000 vehicles daily.

item.title: Uzbekistan Gains Ground in Afghanistan's Flour Market, Kazakhstan Loses Exports
item.description: Uzbekistan is increasing its share in Afghanistan's flour market, while Kazakhstan experiences a decline in its exports. This shift indicates a changing trade dynamic in the region, with implications for agricultural economies.

item.title: Problematic Loans in Uzbek Banks Increase by 33% in Eight Months, State Banks See Faster Growth
item.description: Problematic loans in Uzbekistan's banking sector rose by 33% in the first eight months of the year. State-owned banks experienced a faster increase in non-performing loans, with one bank's overdue debt growing by 1.24 trillion soums.

item.title: World Vision Funds New Water Supply Network in Afghanistan's Faryab Province
item.description: A new water supply network, funded by World Vision International, has been completed in Faryab Province, Afghanistan. The project, costing over 3.4 million Afghanis, will provide 600 families in Khwaja Asfalan village with access to safe drinking water by converting saline water. This initiative addresses the critical lack of clean water in remote Afghan regions.

item.title: French President Macron to Address Nation Amid Widespread Protests and Riots
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation on October 18th following widespread protests and riots that began on October 17th. The protests, involving "Yellow Vest" supporters, students, and unions, saw an estimated 550,000 participants nationwide. The unrest has caused hundreds of millions of euros in damages to businesses.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank New Policy: Expert Analysis on Economic Impact
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has begun cautiously easing its monetary policy, lowering the base rate from 18% to 16.25% by September. Despite improving macroeconomic indicators and falling inflation, experts note that real incomes are stagnant, credit costs remain high, and rapid rate cuts could reignite inflation. The policy's true meaning for the population and economy is under scrutiny.

item.title: New Calculator on eGov Mobile App to Assess Family Welfare
item.description: A new service on the eGov Mobile app allows citizens to assess their family's welfare. Launched as part of a transition to providing state aid based on actual need from January 1, 2027, the calculator evaluates family well-being using over 59 indicators across six areas. It considers income, property, family composition, and the presence of children, elderly, or disabled individuals.

item.title: Kazakhstan Joins Alliance for Protection of Asia's Cultural Heritage
item.description: Kazakhstan has become an observer state in the Alliance for the Protection of Cultural Heritage of Asia following a meeting in China. This status facilitates cooperation with Asian countries in preserving shared cultural legacy. Kazakhstan's participation is seen as a significant step towards strengthening regional cultural ties.

item.title: UNICEF Representative Highlights Need for Quality Medicines in Afghanistan
item.description: Tajudeen Oyewale, UNICEF Afghanistan representative, stressed the critical need for safe, high-quality medicines for Afghan children and families. A meeting with regional pharmaceutical manufacturers in Tashkent aimed to ensure sustainable access to essential medicines amid healthcare challenges in Afghanistan.

item.title: Astana to Complete Approximately 15 Kilometers of New Roads This Year
item.description: Astana Mayor Zhenis Kassymbek announced plans to complete around 15 kilometers of new roads by year-end as part of a comprehensive road infrastructure development. This initiative aims to improve traffic flow and reduce congestion on key routes, including the construction of engineering networks along T Independence Street.

item.title: Afghanistan Sees Surge in Mysterious Killings, Over 70 Deaths Reported in Two Months
item.description: Afghanistan has experienced a significant rise in mysterious killings, with over 70 individuals, including civilians and three Taliban members, reported dead in the past two months. Incidents range from stabbings in Kunar to shootings in Baghlan, with motives often unclear and perpetrators unidentified, raising concerns amid Taliban restrictions on information.

item.title: Dogharoun Border Handles 70% of Iran's Exports to Afghanistan; Regional Transport Projects Discussed
item.description: The Dogharoun border crossing manages 70% of Iran's exports to Afghanistan and significant transit goods. Meanwhile, regional partners met in Astana to advance the Trans-Afghan corridor and CASA railway project, aiming to boost connectivity and trade.

item.title: Kazakh Ambassador Appointed Deputy Secretary General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation
item.description: Kazakh Ambassador Bagdat Amreyev has been elected Deputy Secretary General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) for administrative and financial affairs. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan stated this decision reflects high trust and recognition of Kazakhstan's contribution to multilateral cooperation within the OIC. Kazakhstan reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful conflict resolution through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Cache of Weapons, Including Shotgun and Grenades, Found in Almaty
item.description: Police in Almaty discovered a hidden cache of weapons and ammunition near a road, including a modified shotgun, a pistol-like object, and various ammunition. Grenades and other potentially dangerous items were also seized. An investigation is underway to determine the owner and origin of the weapons, following similar discoveries in the city.

item.title: Turkic States Agree on Information Policy and Media Cooperation in AI Era
item.description: Leaders of media structures from Turkic states convened in Astana for the 8th meeting on information policy and media cooperation in the age of artificial intelligence. The Astana Media Week 2026 international forum also took place, with Uzbekistan represented by the director of the Center for Content Production for Media under the Presidential Administration.

item.title: Astana Mayor Details Major Road Projects to be Completed This Year
item.description: Astana Mayor Zhenis Kassymbek announced that nearly 50 road projects are underway, with plans to complete an additional 15 km of road network by year-end. These projects aim to improve transport accessibility and alleviate congestion in key city areas, including the development of engineering networks along Tаwelsizdik Street.

item.title: Chinese Premier Visits Center for Islamic Civilization in Tashkent
item.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited the Center for Islamic Civilization in Tashkent during his official visit to Uzbekistan. He was briefed on the center's activities and its role in showcasing Uzbekistan's contributions to science and civilization. The visit aimed to strengthen the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Obtains Observer Status in Asian Cultural Heritage Protection Alliance
item.description: Kazakhstan has been granted observer status in the Asian Cultural Heritage Protection Alliance during its 4th Council meeting in Hangzhou, China. The Ministry of Culture and Information reported this development. Vice-Minister Aybek Sydykov proposed cooperation in specialist training, remote monitoring using digital technologies, and joint archaeological research.
